title: Greedy loop and unconditional merge give the same partition
statement: Fix $n \in \bbn$, let $\mathit{es}$ be a list of weighted edges over $n$ vertices, and let $\mathit{uf} : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbn$ be an initial union--find state. The greedy loop, which scans $\mathit{es}$ in order and merges the endpoints of each edge only when they currently carry different representatives, yields a final state that induces the same partition of the vertices as the unconditional fold, which merges the endpoints of every edge of $\mathit{es}$ in order without regard to their current components. That is, for all $i, j : \mathrm{Fin}\,n$, nodes $i$ and $j$ share a representative in the greedy-loop state if and only if they share a representative in the unconditional-fold state.
hypotheses_covered: arbitrary edge list es over n vertices
replaced:
For every edge list and every initial state $uf$, the state
$\texttt{Kruskal.ufAfterProcessEdges}$ produces induces the same partition of the vertices
as merging all the edges unconditionally, i.e.\ it has the same partition as
$uf.\mathrm{mergeAll}$ applied to the whole list.
